subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — follow-up on latency/throughput requirements
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — follow-up on latency/throughput requirements

Hi Tom,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the time and context on BrightCart's plans for real-time recommendations. Quick recap from our discovery so we're aligned and so I can scope the best recommendation:

- Goal: real-time product recommendations surface on product pages and cart in under ~200ms p95.
- Current traffic profile you shared: baseline ~80 req/s, promotional peaks up to ~450 req/s for ~10–20 minute windows.
- Average prompt size: ~60 tokens in / ~40 tokens out.
- No sensitive PII in payloads (confirmed).

Open questions that will help finalize recommendation:
1) During peak windows, is the 450 req/s sustained steady (constant) or bursty/spiky?
2) Do you have a strict p99 SLA or is p95 the primary target?
3) Any regulatory/network constraints (e.g., VPC requirement)?

Initial guidance: if your peaks are short, Hosted API with autoscaling, caching, and batching can often meet tight p95 targets and is fastest to get started. If you have sustained high throughput (hundreds of req/s steady) with strict p95 requirements, Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) gives more consistent tail latency and cost predictability.

I've attached a quick draft proposal and our latency test template so we can validate in your stack. Next steps I propose:
- Confirm answers to the open questions above
- Quick technical call with Marissa (our SE) to size Dedicated and/or plan a Hosted load test
- Pilot options: 2-week Hosted load test vs 30-day Dedicated eval (we can share estimated costs)

Would you be available for a 45-min technical call next week? I can loop Marissa in to go over test payloads and expected latency targets.

Thanks — Neha

Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — follow-up on latency/throughput requirements

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the summary — that matches my notes. Answers below:

1) The 450 req/s during promos tends to be sustained for ~15 minutes; it ramps up over 2–3 minutes and then holds.
2) p95 is primary for UX; p99 we care about but it's not a hard SLA today.
3) No VPC requirement for this product team; however data residency in US only would be ideal.

We'd really like to avoid buying Dedicated unless we have to — main concerns are cost and time to provision. If Hosted can reliably hit ~180–200ms p95 during those 15-minute promo windows, that's ideal. If not, we need to understand the Dedicated pricing and how quickly we could move.

Also: would appreciate any guidance on whether model choice (smaller vs medium vs Llama-class variants) materially changes the recommendation.

Happy to do a tech call — I'm available Thu 22 Apr 9–11am or Mon 26 Apr 1–4pm PT.

Best,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Hosted vs Dedicated — technical sizing notes (internal)

Neha — quick technical notes you can use in the reply to Tom. High-level guidance based on the numbers he gave:

- Hosted behavior: our hosted API autoscaler and routing can handle short promo spikes, but there are limits: for p95 ~200ms with ~60/40 token sizes, Hosted generally works well up to ~100–150 req/s sustained and can handle higher bursty traffic if cache hit rates are good and requests are well distributed. For the 15-min sustained 450 req/s window, Hosted will likely see degraded p95 unless we tune aggressively (very aggressive autoscaling, pre-warming, and high cache hit rates).

- Dedicated behavior: Dedicated with a small reserved pool (2–4 A100-class GPUs or equivalent) will provide much more stable tail latency at 450 req/s sustained. With optimized batching and KV cache, you can target p95 ~120–180ms depending on model choice. Dedicated also gives predictable unit costs for sustained traffic.

- Model choice impact: smaller/quantized variants reduce per-token latency and increase throughput. If the team can accept slightly reduced quality, a quantized medium variant will materially lower the GPU footprint and meet tight p95 targets more easily on Hosted. For full-quality variants (non-quantized), Dedicated is safer.

- Practical steps:
  1) Run a Hosted load test using the attached latency-tests.csv payloads for a 2-week promo simulation (we can help run this in your environment).
  2) If Hosted fails to meet p95 targets, move to a 30-day Dedicated eval — we can spin up a reserved pool and migrate traffic gradually.

- Quick numbers (approx):
  • Hosted: comfortable baseline up to ~150 req/s p95 ~150–220ms with caching; above that depends heavily on cache and autoscale headroom.
  • Dedicated (2x A100): sustained 400–600 req/s with p95 ~120–180ms depending on batching/quantization and prompt size.

I can prep a short slide with expected cost comparisons for 2-week Hosted test vs 30-day Dedicated eval if that helps the exec team.

—Marissa
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

(On internal notes: if we recommend Dedicated, include an option for burst capacity on Hosted as a fallback to smooth unexpected spikes.)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — follow-up on latency/throughput requirements

Hi Tom — thanks for the details and availability. Quick summary and two proposed paths so we can move forward:

Option A — Hosted pilot (fastest):
- Run a targeted 2-week Hosted load test using your promo traffic pattern (we'll use the attached payloads).
- We instrument p95/p99, cache hit rates, and autoscale behavior. If we can meet ~180–200ms p95 consistently, you stay on Hosted.
- Pros: fastest to start, no upfront commit; Cons: risk of degraded p95 during sustained 15-min windows if cache/autoscale doesn't hold.

Option B — Dedicated eval (predictable):
- 30-day Dedicated eval (2x A100-class GPUs recommended) with migration plan and rollback to Hosted for bursts.
- Pros: predictable tail latency and unit cost for sustained traffic; Cons: longer provisioning time and commitment.

Model choice: if you can tolerate some quality tradeoffs, a quantized medium variant reduces latency and makes Hosted more likely to meet p95 targets. If quality must be preserved, Dedicated is the safer choice.

Next steps:
1) Which option would you prefer to start with (Hosted pilot vs Dedicated eval)?
2) If Hosted pilot, can you confirm exact promo schedule so we can schedule the test to coincide?
3) If Dedicated eval, I'll put together a short cost / timeline estimate and kick off provisioning.

I've attached the draft proposal and latency test CSV again for your review. Marissa — feel free to add any scheduling notes or cost bullets.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this validated in your environment.
